resources.string: AWG is a geometric series, not a scale: the number falls as the conductor grows, and the sizes above 0 are written 00, 000 and 0000 — enter those as −1, −2 and −3. Because the defining formula is continuous, a metric cross-section can convert to a gauge between two real sizes; round to the next larger conductor, which is the lower number.
The International Table calorie of 4.1868 J is used, to agree with the IT British thermal unit in the same category. The thermochemical calorie of 4.184 J is 0.07 % smaller.

Horsepower comes in two sizes: mechanical hp is 550 ft·lbf/s, metric PS is 75 kgf·m/s, and they differ by about 1.4 %. Motor nameplates in Europe usually mean PS. Both are offered rather than one being chosen for you.
A circular mil is the area of a circle one thousandth of an inch across, so kcmil is an area and converts exactly. 4/0 AWG is 211.6 kcmil is 107.2 mm² — three ways of writing the same conductor.

Temperature is the one category that is not proportional: 20 °C is not twice 10 °C, because the scales place their zero somewhere other than absolute zero. Conversions here account for the offset, so a temperature difference must not be converted as if it were a temperature.

Volt-amperes are deliberately absent from the power category. Apparent power converts to watts only through the power factor, and treating 1 kVA as 1 kW would be wrong on every load that is not purely resistive. Use the power calculator for that relationship.
